txt: *"What?"* She chortles, nearly spilling her tea.
...for about half a minute -- in silence.
...then secures the mooring line. "It's good to see you here, detective. I only just arrived myself."
...then secures the mooring line. "It's good to see you here, detectives. I only just arrived myself."
...then to the east, toward the harbour: "And that is the terminal. Another subdivision deals with energy -- oil and gas exploration. Offshore platforms."
A smirk passes her face. "I think I'll stick with the factory name. But thank you."
A striking woman leans against the cabin top of her sailing boat, smiling as you approach. Her green raincoat glistens with droplets, a silk scarf is tied around her throat.
A well-kempt, yet tastefully short bob of dark hair. Despite the first hints of grey, she's elected to keep it au naturale -- shaped into a permanent wave, late-Forties style...
Another woman gone.
Her eyes go round with surprise. "And what would *that* be?"
Her eyes return to you. "It isn't enough to call us animals. Even animals aren't animals."
Her mouth is relaxed, the accordion lines near her mouth vanish. The pearls of her eyes move slowly on the photo's surface.
Her voice is almost wistful. "We could have had so much *more*. Every one of us -- if only we'd played it right."
Seaweed drips from the badge in your hand. It smells of fish. "What can I help you with, lieutenant-yefreitor?"
She clasps her thermal cup, uncertain.
She clears her throat. "Now, how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
She closes her eyes and breathes out heavily: "... the most *disco* thing you will ever see."
She closes her eyes, trying to picture the man's face... then shakes her head...
She considers taking a sip. She doesn't.
She continues: "The literage the local producers must get from this terminal alone must be *oceanic*."
She enjoys a small sip.
She gives the material another pat. "What I *can* do for you is answer some *questions*. Nothing like talking to pass a rainy day."
She hands it back to you. "Pleased to meet you, Lieutenant Double-Yefreitor Du Bois. I am glad to see a man of high qualification -- the situation is precarious."
She hands it back to you: "It is a relief to see a double-yefreitor here. The situation is precarious to say the least. It needs a quick solution, or we will have a blood bath on our hands."
She hands you back the photo. "Is there anything else I can help you with?"
She is silent for a moment, then concludes: "As I said -- a blood bath."
She laughs out loud. It is a beautiful laugh, laced with glee and a certain sharpness. It travels far on the water...
She lets out an unrestrained laugh, the crows feet stretching onto her cheeks...
She looks at you, expectantly. It is as if you have said nothing -- because you have not. No begging words have left your mouth...
She looks beyond you, despondent.
She looks positively surprised. "That's great. For the investigation, I mean."
She looks up: "It's like the crowning of the world. It's insane. Very *disco*. You'd love it."
She nods and returns the plastic bag to her coat.
She nods attentively.
She nods politely. "Of course. Any more questions about the boat, sir?"
She nods, attentively.
She nods, carefully, as though handling a match near a powder keg. "Such referrals may sometimes get you information from a man like Evrart," she says, raising an eyebrow. "Did it?"

She nods, forcefully: "There are no minor cogs in the system. Each terminal must be accounted for, lest the entire system break. Every hiccup in such a system means thousands lose their jobs -- the world over. I'm here to assure that doesn't happen."
She nods, slowly.
She nods. "I'm glad to hear, officer. I'm sure you'll find out just what that means, soon enough."
She nods. "It may be the only *break* we've ever caught as a species. The last one for four hundred years."
She nods. "Sensible for her to disable access to such essential information."
She nods. "That is only fair."

She nods. "The phenomenon has never again been encountered. For a time the crew thought they were experiencing a hallucination. The mast-hand proclaimed 'L´Insulinde! L´Insulinde!' -- the signal to wake up."
She nods. "There was no precedent for such an undertaking. People thought she was punishing the admirals, or had gone mad, or both..."
She nods.
She nods: "I hope I can be of help."
She observes your eyes scanning the horizon, then breaks the silence, slowly.

She opens them: "This place used to be a province, a workers' resort before the city swallowed it and the artillery did its work. The reeds are the real star of the show here now. The further down the coast, the wilder it gets."
She pauses to take a long, leisurely sip of tea. "Alright, what next?"
She puts her hand in the rain. She's silent for a second.
She quietly nods. "You have my full cooperation."
She reaches for the photo; takes it, then holds it in her hand...
She reconsiders that sip.
She remains unfazed. "That is precisely what the sailors feared when they drew these maps. A fear of drowning -- within one's own corpse."
She removes a few notes and hands them to you. The paper is cold and oily to the touch.

She shakes her head vigorously. "My plan is to share information. The only way to do that *now* is by telling my employers you've kept your end. Which I hope you will, because let me tell you: we are in *dire* waters."
She simply nods.
She sips from her thermos. She does not look away from you.
She sips from her thermos.
She smells the cold air, then withdraws her hand slowly.
She smiles. "Watch out for yourself. They will strike soon."
She smiles. "Watch out for yourselves. They will strike soon."
She stares at you, head tilted to the side, with a slightly concerned look on her face.
She takes a sip of tea. "Now, is there anything I can do for you in the meanwhile? Tea, perhaps?"
She takes a sip.
She thinks. "But yes, you'll be fine, don't worry."
She turns to him. "And what is *your* official position, lieutenant?"
She's looking out toward the sea, what at, it's hard to say.
She's silent a moment, contemplating. When she finally speaks, her tone is wistful: "We could have had so much *more*. Every one of us -- if only we'd played it right."
She's silent. The wind flaps the sail above her.
She's silent.
She's tying a complicated nautical knot around the post.
Silence. She lowers her hand.
The wind blows, waves crash in the distance. She crosses her arms and asks: "Did I ever tell you how they discovered this isola? During our talks?"
The woman -- born in the year 3 in the Commune of Revachol -- smiles at you, face adorned with frown lines and crow's feet. The photo is recent. The name reads Rejoyce Leyton-Messier.

The woman is silent, smiling while the waves lap against the hull. In your hand, under the plastic -- a light blue passport saying *REPUBLIC OF VESPER*. The coat of arms has a lion and an ostrich, sejant.
The woman is tying a complicated nautical knot around the post, while occasionally exchanging a few words with the other woman.
The woman is tying a complicated nautical knot around the post.
The woman on the boat does not notice her staring.
The woman scans her surroundings as though a neurologist might magically appear.
While dull orange pearls hang from her ear lobes, red from cold. Her light green eyes scan you, full of knowledge -- and worry. Wealth and all its possibilities.
Why yes! Tucked away under that sturdy green raincoat, almost rustic in its simplicity -- a silk shirt and matching scarf around her gentle throat...
You leave her fastening the mooring line around the post rotting in the water.
You're poor. Poor as balls. You can't ask this person for money. You're too...
"'*Après la vie, la mort*,' they summarized it for the queen and Dolores Dei; '*Après la mort, la vie encore! Après le monde, le gris. Après le gris, le monde encore!*'"
"'Every worker a member of the board'. I tried to convince my employer it was simply a piece of rhetoric and not a serious demand. But the... *stridency* of it seems to have spooked them."
"'Fuck off, midget.' Gaumont is short of stature, you see."
"'Spying' has such a negative connotation. I did track your progress along the coast, however, and decided I would be better able to assist you from here..."
"*...a member of the board*," she nods. "I tried to convince my employer it was simply a piece of rhetoric -- or a joke. They did not appreciate the humour."
"*A Deuill*," she pronounces: "*Who being of great Charme and Guille, sneaketh into the homes of the Godlie*."
"*All* of them."
"*And* in the process you turned up some information relevant to your investigation. Only from Evrart, surprisingly!"
"*Beyond* curious. I will *choose* to interpret that as you turning the alcohol in the strike brew *down* -- for the sake of our professional relationship."
"*EVERY WORKER -- A MEMBER OF THE BOARD!*"

"*Entroponetics*," she corrects, "is the scientific study of the pale. Or a recent iteration of it, by way of Graad. The study of the pale reaches back 6,000 years -- the Perikarnassians called it the Western Plain."

"*Isola* is a Messinian word for a continent of matter, enveloped on all sides by the pale. Also: isolation, or land mass. We used to believe there was only one. In the last four centuries we have discovered seven..."
"*Joyce* is much more efficient."
"*Krenel* -- an Oranjese military company. As far as I know three arrived in Martinaise. They report to me sporadically, but they do not answer to me. To be frank, our relationship is deteriorating."
"*Liked* is a bit strong," she tosses her head. "He... he was the most charismatic among them. He handled all the talking. His departure left a major gap in the group's *communication skills*."
"*Many* bleak scenarios have already come to pass to lead us here..." She looks at you, eyes damp from the wind.
"*Oh*. And what happened to it, detective?" She returns the lieutenant's badge.
"*Oh*. And what happened to yours, detective?" She returns the lieutenant's badge and turns to you.
"*Or* you can find your badge, which, honestly, seems like a lost cause."
"*Or*..." She picks the cup back up. "You can recover your badge -- though if I may be blunt with you, it sounds like that may be a lost cause."
"*Powerful*..."

"*Precisely*. Someone needs to move the ingredients *from* the harbour into the city. Once they reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they are *vulnerable*."
"*Precisomundo*!"
"*Taking* it..." She looks toward the colourful mountain of crates, like toy blocks rising above Martinaise.
"... then for my daughters'. We had an obligation to defend our sovereignty. We should have *burned* the whole isola down rather than let them have it."
"...and if the law officials of our nation need help with the basic terms of reality -- well, then I am here to help." She bows.
"...how could I stop you? Are we not human? Are we not *curious* to hear another person's take? It's only natural. We would only be..." she smiles, "gossiping."
"...maybe there is something else I can assist you with? While you're *hot* in pursuit?"
"...or two." She looks around.
"...steal, kill and destroy?" She counters, quick as a whip. "That they say we've been doing for over four decades now. Perhaps regrettably, I've had my fill for this century..."
"...you have me -- I will assist you in any way I can. Even if we have to do it one basic term at a time." She gives you a slight bow.
"33A -- this old *proletarian* haunt here." She waves at the ruin looming overhead. "As I said, *plenty* of people drive boats. Of all social strata."
"A *fishery*. I've been speaking with Lilienne here. She gave me the idea. The infrastructure is all here, and with my connections..."
"A *she...*" The negotiator does not seem to be shocked at first.
"A Villiers 9mm, front loaded? Two or three barrelled..."
"A bird?" She tilts her head. "A *sphenicid* -- a flightless bird of the polar regions?"
"A casual term of endearment popular among the 50+ crowd. It's a disco holdover, pay it no heed."
"A city state divided into free market zones. Under the *everlasting* interregnum of the Coalition of Nations. And you, of course -- the Citizens Militia."

"A company getaway. For a weekend or a summer holiday. Then came the Revolution, but that's another matter..." She takes a sip. "I'm here to make sure the Pines can fulfil their responsibilities to the place they *built*."
"A confrontation is imminent. They have followed in your footsteps..."
"A conglomerate the size of Wild Pines is like a shark -- if it stops moving and growing it will die. Then what becomes of those 72,000 families? It is a tremendous responsibility."
"A conglomerate the size of the Wild Pines is like a shark -- if it stops moving it will die. Then what becomes of those 72,000 families? It's a tremendous responsibility."
"A deep synthesis," she nods. "I'll assist you however I can then. Go ahead. Ask."
"A devout man of the centre," she nods. "Hard to come by. It's good to have someone who takes a moderate approach to head-shooting -- in your line of work I mean."
"A first-rate find -- that should tell you all you need to know about their network, I would imagine."
"A fitting punishment," she smirks. "To be forgotten, if not forgiven. Save a prayer for us in our *châteaus* on Ozonne and in Stella Maris."
"A giant statue of him or, better yet, his twin brother. Practically the same thing, but makes him seem less like a psychopath."
"A lot of it," she nods. "It comes in from large Samaran factories. In South Safre, Siigay and Hsin-Yao. The literage they must get from this terminal alone must be *oceanic*."
"A pleasure to meet you, Harry -- what happened to your badge?"
"A poor remedy for prion disease," she says. "That was the attitude of most of the more moderate indotribes, particularly those who supported the king..."

"A pre-revolutionary tenement. Old buildings are called *tenements*, you see, and new buildings *batiments*, after *les batiments noveau*. But 33A and 33B are not *noveau*, they're old." She looks up at the crumbling facade...
"A referral, you mean? I take it this was for someone in the RCM..." She waves her hand. "Don't answer that."
"A runaway? Good work, this is a tangible lead towards solving the whole mystery."
"A she..." She raises a brow. "I hope she wasn't too serious a suspect. If she got away..."
"A smart boy getting smarter, one basic term of reality at a time..."
"A sort of... spiritual quest? Something of ancient Iilmaraan origin?" There's more than a trace of irony in her voice.
"A stroke could partially explain the *memory trouble* you've been experiencing."
"A takeover?"
"A term of hatred that originates, like many such things, with the Mesque petrofascists."

"A total shift," she nods. "In human comprehension of reality. On the second day, a great skua was shot down, above the flagship Lysergique. The bird was preserved and brought back. Along with pollen."
"A youth centre with Edgar Claire's statue on top of it!" She looks down the jetty, remorsefully.
"A youth centre with Edgar Claire's statue on top of it..." Her eyes run across the water, remorsefully.
"About head-shooting?" She smiles.
"About the boat?" A wisp of steam rises from her thermal cup.
"About what?"
"Absolutely -- my commitment here is long term."
"Absolutely not. These mercenaries are muscle, pure and simple. They are meant to intimidate the Union into surrendering."
"Achromatic, odourless, featureless. The pale is the enemy of matter and life. It is not *like* any other -- or *any* thing in the world. It is the transition state of being into nothingness."
"Actually, yes. The thought did cross my mind when Mademoiselle Lilienne earlier told me about the fresh produce these women sell to restaurants on the Delta."
"Actually, yes. The thought did cross my mind when Mademoiselle Lilienne over there told me about the fresh produce these women sell to restaurants on the Delta."
"Actually," she turns to the lieutenant, "I've heard the analogy made by a blindingly modern school of philosophy called *karperie*. It may not be as far fetched as it sounds."
"Ah yes, I've been meaning to go there..." She looks over the bay.
"Ah yes, of course, I'm sad to hear that." She nods, as if its self explanatory. "How much do you need?"
"Ah yes, your condition. The International Collaboration Police maintains a database for these sorts of things. Perhaps you should consult it. It was just a suggestion."
"Ah yes. As you said." She looks confused for a moment.
"Ah!" She spreads her arms almost as wide. "*This* is the pier of Rue de Saint-Ghislaine 33A, where the tenants have been kind enough to rent me a slot..."
"Ah, good to hear. I wouldn't want to pry into a confidential police matter. But, in the event you'd like to share more... I *would* like to know who it was."
"Ah, yes -- back to the *low-down*."
"Ah, yes -- the *episode*. Sounds like an acute case of encephalopathy now that I think of it..." She puts down her thermal cup and looks at you.
"Ah, yes. That is what counts, I suppose. For my part, I was more of a *New* girl."
"Ah, yes. There's something very satisfying about discussing the fundamental facts of reality. Go ahead."
"Ah, yes..." She looks hesitant. "This is not very *central* to reality, is it?"
"Ah, you know more than you let on..." She gives you a coy little smile. "Philosopher-Detective of Precinct 41."
"All men are predators, dear. Nothing much to be done about *that*. It's all a matter of where you get to file your teeth..."

"All the best parts of it. Rue de Saint-Ghislaine with its bastions, the plaza's Meteoran mosaic. Even some of the old street lamps have been put back thanks to investments from the WP." She points behind you where the seawall rises.
"All we can do is keep that which has not from following suit. One single, concrete suspect delivered into Civil Court -- and I *may* be able to defuse this situation."
"All we can do is keep the little that has not from following suit. One single, concrete suspect delivered into Civil Court -- and I *may* be able to defuse this situation."
"All we can do is keep the rest from following suit. One single, concrete suspect delivered into Civil Court -- and I *may* be able to defuse this situation."
"All we can do is keep the rest from going the same way. One single, concrete suspect delivered into Civil Court -- and I *may* be able to defuse this situation."
"All yours?" She nods. "That's been the motto of many an indotribe. There is something *clarifying* about that strain of ultraliberalism..."
"Always," She nods. "That's the *can't-do-attitude* that truly defines Late Modernity. You may prove a Modern Man yet."
"An almost endearingly moralist standpoint," she bows. "It must be hard to take a moderate approach to head-shooting in your line of work."
"An insane goal." Her eyes return to you. "Krenel has a thousand men on their payroll. The next batch will be a platoon of twenty men and a gunship, the one after that, a hundred."
"An insane goal." Her eyes return to you. "Krenel has a thousand men on their payroll. The next batch will be a platoon of twenty men and a gunship. You can't simply *trick* them."
"An intuitive conclusion of that development is that one day the pale will cover everything -- but this sort of talk is mostly left to extremists."
"An oceanic isola. It comprises mostly of water. Mundi is the largest, Katla the coldest, Insulinde the bluest. What can I say..." She stops. "Each is perishing and dear."
"An ominous vision..." She nods solemnly. "At least you understand the gravity of the situation. And the maps should prove very valuable indeed."
"An ultraliberal, it's a type of liberal. From the Revolution. It's... not the moderate kind."
"An uproar of matter, darling, *rising* into the pale. Rolling. Evaporating even, a great vision. The area of transition between the world and the pale is called *porch collapse*."
"And *now* people are getting *lynched*, I hear. Behind the Whirling-in-Rags... a disastrous situation if there ever was one."
"And I asked *you*, past-less detective of the Citizens Militia. What insight has acute encephalopathy given to you?"
"And I asked *you*, philosopher-detective of the Citizens Militia."
"And because I don't like the idea of them any more drunk than they already are." She nods. "What else?"
"And even *if* I did I still would not give you ten thousand reál. I would rather buy something nice with it. Like expensive hi-fi or a new *Hydrodynamique E40* sail."
"And here I thought my modest payment of 100 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"And here I thought my modest payment of 130 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"And here I thought my modest payment of 30 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"And here I thought my modest payment of 40 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"And here I thought my modest payment of 70 reál would stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"And if he does not change course it will be a war negotiation, detective."
"And if those authorities drink so hard they need help recalling the basic terms of reality -- well, I am here to help." She bows and smiles.
"And to think -- there are years when the group books *losses* in the billions..." A wave hits the sloop, she grasps the mainstay for balance.

"And you too, lieutenant," she turns to him and stresses: "The situation is perilous, but I am *sure* you're dedicated to avoiding further loss of life. Unlike the Union, who won't even let me talk to them."
"And your opinion, detective? If I may ask. I'm a curious and talkative person you see," she explains." Would you say the Débardeurs' Union is..."
"Anxious to hear more about mineral rights or who got shot in the head?" A flash of teeth in her feisty grin.
"Anyway, enough sentimentality. Is there anything else you want to know?"
"Anyway," she concludes. "What other basic facets of reality should we discuss?"

"Are you *liberated* enough to offer up your home on a plate for financial colonists?" She looks you in the eye. "No, I think not. Tell me -- now that I've *uncoiled* myself -- do you find me frightening?"
"Are you satisfied, detective? What else can you tell me about your *mail delivery quest* for Evrart? Do you think it will *improve* the place?"
"Are you sure you're sure? Your colleague seemed adamant..."

"As I was saying..." Her voice breaks the silence and suddenly you're back again. Nearby, a seagull pecks at a piece of garbage... "If there's *any* way I may be of assistance, please don't hesitate to ask."
"As eager as I am to *share* it, lieutenant, once the job is done."
"As they do."
"As your investigation reaches a climax, so does theirs. They are your shadow. Arm yourselves. Armour yourselves..."
"At least not in the same *manner and volume* as the others do. They are the long-standing provisional rulers of Revachol now -- the Coalition Government."
"Au contraire, officer. I also feel queasy about the pittance the Coalition calls your salary. Now is there something else I can do for you, or did you want to chat about *dialectics* some more?"
"Be my guest." She takes a sip from her thermal cup.
"Because it was manufactured in Revachol East by a company called Cor-de-Leite, and it's hull is '19 paces long."

"Before Martinaise was swallowed by the industrial harbour, even before it was part of Revachol -- long before Terminal B was erected here -- the Pines built it as a resort for its Revacholian employees."
"Believe it or not, Wild Pines isn't even the most notorious example -- that would be Saint-Baptiste. You can go quite far with that attitude."
"Better not to tie the forestay to the backstay on this. I hope there is something else I can help you with?"
"Beyond curious... Tell me -- what do you *think* of the pale?"
"Brinkmanship -- or sabre-rattling... Was he surrounded by *Union men* he wanted to impress?"
"But -- I am derailing us. You wanted to know about the strike."
"But -- I won't pry further about the case. You mentioned something about Mr. Claire, I believe? Or something in conjunction with the Union? I might have gotten the wrong idea, but..."
"But -- this is one of the great questions of our time. Maybe when they get the complete set together it will jolt us out of our rut -- bring us together. However naive it may sound."
"But it is still hard for humans to navigate the pale without getting lost. Or having our minds damaged."
"But then, I'm no doctor." She takes a long sip of tea. "Ask away, officer -- I'll help however I can."

"But these others weren't uninhabited. We had to kill people there, wipe out indigenous populations, gunboat economies. Or they came to do the same for us. Or had done to each other. But here..." she spreads her arms.

"But they could not. They were sane and conscious, as islands began to appear on the horizon... There are 78,000 uninhabited islands in the Insulindian archipelago, officer. The freckled face of god," she smiles.
"But what was done exactly? Revolution, the rise and crash of capital, international intervention..."
"But you already have," she looks around. "And you're doing just fine, despite the rubble."
"By love, you did!" She inspects the piece of blue plastic, her eyes scanning from left to right.
"By that I mean conflicts. Ideological conflicts. The stuff of men."

"Caillou." She looks to the waters. "Imagine a pebble, a smoothed over pebble amidst a great blue sea. Mis-shapen, cracked. The cracks are the River Esperance. We're in the delta of this river, on the sixth branch -- the Martinaise distributary."
"Capital *is* finished. But understand this -- its end won't *free* anyone. It will only lead to more suffering."

"Centuries of care, deliberation -- and *madness* -- have gone into this endeavour. Vessels pass through the Great Unrest to re-emerge with apricots in tow. The logic of the system is totalizing... It's taken *everything* from its employees to build it."
"Charmed, enchanted, put under his spell."
"Clean, yes. Nothing will grow here for twenty years. Krenel will send in gunships and the Coalition Government will follow suit."
"Clever. Few suspect a woman in this sort of skulduggery. Good move on their part."

"Close," she nods. "Port cities. This is an Oranjese Map of the Waterways -- a sailor's tattoo worn by wayfarers of the Dolorian century, over 300 years ago. The sailors would mark their bodies to map their travels."
"Come now. Nobody carries that much cash on their person, particularly in a place like Martinaise... I'd get robbed."
"Corruption! That's how he's done it. Fantastic, würm-like corruption reaching into the bowels of the Earth." She looks at the ground and nods.
"Coupris, Resplendent... both gone now. Those that survived mended their ways. They're all *ultras* now."
"Detective? Is everything alright in there?"
"Did he now?" Her eyes narrow. "Well, then it should be any day now. Unless, of course, he's *lying* to you. Anyway, was there anything else you've heard?"
"Did they ever. Before they got shot themselves, they shot two million people."
"Did you now?" She's intrigued, if a little confused. "What sort of borscht is he making?"
"Did you? Wonderful!" She inspects the piece of blue plastic, the faded green pearls of her eyes scanning left to right.
"Do not gloat, officer. These are grave matters."

"Do not spend 22 days a year in pale transit, don't waste your twenties slumming it with your stupid friends, and don't deliver Evrart Claire's mail." Her bony finger is pointed like an arrow at your chest...
"Do what you have to do, detective. I don't think deciphering that tattoo should come before public security. But if you should wade into the mob to find out -- I couldn't stop you."
"Do you know how they discovered this place?" The wind picks up, her raincoat flaps in the gust.
"Do you think it's within my authority to give it to them? Do you think I can control the board and the shell-shocked mercenaries they've sent?"
"Do you want me to take you to a hospital, sir?"
"Does it?" She arches her brow. "The company suspects foul play, but there's nothing they could do, it was a Union matter."

"Don't worry about that one article, dear -- regional papers are useless anyway. You probably spared the man his kneecaps. And *I* can be sure that the local shops have a bone to pick with Evrart." She smiles.
"Don't worry, I'll never get around to it -- the information you pass to me will remain confidential," She waves you off: "Let's get back to reality, shall we?"
"Don't worry, Kras Mazov shot fifteen million people in the head. But that was all the way over in Graad."
"Don't worry. It's curable -- with *questions*. Ask me some, it'll help pass this night."
"Doubtless I'll be off some place, keeping social classes from each other's throats..." There's a pause. "Let's go back to the basics of reality, shall we?"
"Downright *haunting* if you ask me. The Wild Pines suspected foul play, but what could they do? It was a Union matter."
"Drinking less sounds like a great start!" She nods approvingly, but without condescension. "Go on -- you have my full cooperation."
"Edgar looks *exactly* like his brother, except for that lazy eye. He also *talks* exactly like Evrart does. And when one's term as foreman is up, the other takes over."
"Either way, he's alleged to have sexually assaulted a woman. Sometime later a group of dockworkers got their hands on him..."
"Elysium."
"Even if we have to do it one basic term at a time." She gives you a slight bow.
"Everything affects the decision making process, detective."
"Everything." She smiles. "Right up to -- but not including -- *trade secrets*."
"Evrart Claire is a man of the *utmost* integrity. If you can say one thing about him, it's that he always puts the interests of the workers first."
"Excellent." She takes a long sip of tea. "According to my reports there are at least three lorry drivers lingering near the roundabout. Hopefully one of them will know something."
"Excuse me sir, I don't have a billion reál."
"Excuse me, I didn't hear you." Her voice is kind, a little hoarse from the wind.
"Excuse me, I didn't hear you." her voice is kind, a little hoarse from the wind. "Did you say *money*?"
"Extensively."
"Familiar faces."

"Sadly, the company records do not even give a name. She's just *forewoman*, in private correspondence: Holly. I don't even know if it's a sur- or given name. And I don't have access to the Unions' files."
"See? Everyone finds something worth holding onto in the world -- however wasted its opportunities."
"See? Everyone finds something worth holding onto in this world -- however wasted its opportunities."
"Shall we talk about something else maybe?" Her voice is kind, if anything she sounds a little confused.
"She could easily just..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
"She prefers a fantasy world -- an *infraculture* with its own dress code and vernacular. It is an illusion, I'm afraid. There is no refuge from the supraculture."
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 100 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 130 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 30 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 40 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Side-shifting? Of course, *that's* why my payment of 70 reál didn't stick..." She shakes her head in mock regret.
"Silly nostalgia..."
"Slowly raining down until it formed a vast ocean."
"So I hoped." She nods. "But this type of opening is usually followed by a more reasonable offer. I have yet to hear one, just the same nonsensical slogan repeated over and over again..."
"So a quarter of humanity..." she calculates, "...simply lost their minds? And how would you stop a prion -- a complex folding protein; *un-life* -- with the technology 50 years ago?"
"So am I -- and I *do* know how to use one..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
"So this goes *beyond* Jamrock... she looks inland. "At least you now understand the gravity of the situation. And those maps should prove very valuable indeed."
"So very, very helpful," she repeats. "And how is that going? Do you have any *leads* on that gun?"
"So would I -- but woe! There is no such denomination."
"So, permit me to conclude with this -- *who* you are -- to me -- is the police. The only legitimate law enforcement authority in Revachol."
"So," she returns the zip bag to her jacket. "I hope I didn't just *bribe* you, officer. It may not be technically *illegal* under the Emergency Act, but still..."
"Some *arlecchinos* you say?" She shakes her head. "I'm afraid what I need to tell you is anything but *fun* I really need to discuss it, however. With the RCM -- and I need your badge for that."
"Some say the damage stems from extreme sensory deprivation. Others argue that pale somehow *consists* of past information, that's degrading. That it's rarefied past, not rarefied matter."
"Some sort of... krill hunter? No, wait..." Joyce raises her eyebrows. "You're an ancient ruin, a symbol of hubris and decay, half-submerged in some salty sea."
"Some were rich enough to stay with the Constitution; with monarchy -- *big mistake*. Others bet on the Revolution, they were called the Ultras, or ultraliberals. They fared well."
"Somehow I doubt that lecturing them on the legitimate use of force will persuade them to stand down."
"Soon. I do not know precisely. They have cut off all communication, you see. They know I've been feeding you information."
"Sorry," she breaks her concentration. "I was trying to see if I can read the web of interdependencies between these points -- the stars." She points to one on the photo paper.
"Sounds like he has you running errands, detective. A well-established dominance ritual..." She thinks. "Where did he have you deliver it?"
"Speak for yourself, officer. I'm well known in certain parts. As to the place, you're right. We are..." She points across the water, where the skyscrapers rise...

"Steel yourself, officer," she says in a reassuring manner. "Your colleague, Lieutenant Kitsuragi -- he is competent. I checked up on him. And you also have me -- I will try to assist you in any way I can."
"Stupendous!" She nods, more than a bit surprised. "I didn't think he'd pull through."
"Stupendous." She takes a little bow. "Pulling one on the old würm. Commendably done. And... did this trick  yield anything interesting? I assume it was necessary -- for the case..."
"Such a thing isn't in my character."
"Such a tough guy." She gives you a crooked smile. "You have my full cooperation, tough guy -- and that of the Wild Pines Group."
"Such an acute encephalopathy... just doesn't seem possible." She puts her beverage down and stares at you. "Surely you're joking..."
"Surely you're aware that under the Wayfarer Act the RCM doesn't have the authority to demand anyone's operator license. Freedom of movement and all that."

"Surely you're joking. These people are killers. My only hope is that yours provides a single, concrete suspect -- before they indiscriminately pick theirs. Simply put..." She grabs hold of the mainsail:
"Sweetheart, please stop repeating that now." Her eyes look worried, frightened even.
"Taking it out of commission will deal a blow to the smuggling network. Excellent work."
"Technically speaking, you *don't*."
"Ten of the fourteen indotribes got it wrong: Feld, Coupris, Tricentennial... So I suppose I would have been in good company."
"Thank god -- and indeed *Mr. Evrart* as well. In this investigation one may have *use* for a firearm -- you wouldn't want to get caught with your pants down..."
"Thank you -- I do what I can to remain presentable. Now, ask me some questions. It'll help us pass the night."
"Thank you for being candid," she nods. "Sadly, Wild Pines have cooperated with what amounts to a crime syndicate for two decades. However much you feed the wolf -- the wolf always hungers."
"Thank you for the suggestion. I see the word has emotional resonance for you. For me, sadly -- none. So I will stick with the factory name."
"That *would* afford a good vantage point," she says. "In any case, it's practically inaccessible."
"That *would* afford a good vantage point." She nods, poised and unperturbed. "*Still* -- I hope you heed my advice. There's no need to kick the hornet's nest."
"That is a *bad* idea, one I won't be a party to." She shakes her head emphatically.
"That is exactly what it means. What I am about to tell you is more pressing, I assure you."

"That makes sense to me. We have no more use for a Map of the Waterways. Just like we don't need sailors the way we used to. This is what the custom would morph into on the Occident -- mercenary tattoos."
"That may be so." She is poised and unperturbed. "I still hope you heed my advice -- there's no need to kick the hornet's nest."
"That may well be. It's not up to me to decide who is king. But as negotiations go -- it's not a swell start."
"That seems... unlikely."
"That speaks of the vastness and sophistication of the operation. Were you able to examine the radio?"
"That the man was killed because he assaulted a local woman. I've asked around a bit -- this seems to be the accepted story around Martinaise."
"That they don't..." She leans against the railing, looking up at the grey sky.
"That was the annual revenue of the *entire* Wild Pines Group, not my personal fortune..."
"That would explain why the Whirling-in-Rags -- where the Union congregates -- is the *only* bar left open in Martinaise. Well that and Frittte because..."
"That's a good question, officer. I don't have the slightest idea. As I said, it's a rumour -- about a rumour. In any case, it's what the colonel's remaining... colleagues... believe."
"That's a good sum -- not too small, not fantastically large." She reaches into her raincoat and pulls out a zip bag -- in it you see paper notes arranged like black gills.
"That's a pity," she bows. "I hope we can remain collegial despite my monstrousness. The ultras didn't have anything against the king *or* the Commune, you see. It was just business."
"That's a reasonable sum -- not too small, not fantastically large." She reaches into her raincoat and pulls out a zip bag -- in it you see paper notes arranged like black gills.
"That's beautiful..." She inspects it.
"That's garbage! You're a police officer."
"That's good to hear, detective. Police work is rarely pretty, but it sounds like you did what you had to do."
"That's heartening to hear. There are too few honourable men in Revachol." She gives you a slight bow. "Now how else can I help the RCM today, besides supplementing its salaries?"
"That's looking less and less likely, detective. You wouldn't know it from the tabloids, but the ORG nations have been launching weather balloons into the lower ionosphere since the Thirties."
"That's not Coupris, dear. It's just a brand name, snatched up by a Vespertine holding company. No, the real Coupris is as dead as the king they bet on."
"That's right -- the negation of being." She tightens her hood around her neck, it's cold outside.
"That's right. We're all answerable to someone."
"That's the man who was killed..." She almost takes the photo -- but then stops. "I'm afraid this is a discussion for once we've cleared the lynching question."
"That's the way of History." She nods.
"That's wise," she nods. "Our goal is to *avert* catastrophe. Besides," she sighs, "You're likely to encounter them sooner or later."
"The *Ex-* something? The *Ex-* what?"
"The *Great* kind."

"The *lorries,*" she stresses. "Someone needs to move the ingredients from the harbour into the city. Once they reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they are *vulnerable*."
"The *performative experience* has ended. Good -- what can I help you with?"
"The Coalition of Nations. Graad, Mesque, Vesper, Messina, Oranje and Sur-La-Clef -- the armed centre of the world. They landed here and ended the Revolution. It was the *moralist* thing to do."
"The Débardeurs' Union was once a perfectly normal institution. Twenty years ago, anyway. It must *not* have been easy to establish under the Emergency Act, but they did it. I can respect that."
"The New, a cultural era -- and the name of the decade it ravished, the Thirties. It came out of post-revolutionary Revachol. It was... ultraliberal."

"The Pines' *core competency* is logistics -- container shipping, freight, that sort of thing." She points to the small dots on the horizon. "See those airships there, blinking? Those are the shipping side of things..."

"The RCM's responsibilities are defined by the Emergency, Wayfarer, and Aliments Acts -- three pieces of legislation keeping the city in a -- let's be honest -- laissez-faire stasis to the benefit of foreign capital."
"The Revolution began in '02, on the isola of Graad, though by the end nearly the whole world had gotten involved."
"The Revolution," she says.

"The Thirties? Things settled down in the Thirties. Revachol East transformed itself into the world's largest tax haven -- with the international community's blessing. For the first time in a long time it seemed like things were *going* somewhere."
"The Turn-of-the-Century Revolution?" She smiles, mischievously. "Don't answer it -- it's a trick question."
"The Twenties saw a decade of urban war: West of the river levelled, offshore platforms in flames... Still, it's regarded as an improvement on what came before: '08 to '19 was simply hell..."
"The Union is conducting drug trade out of the harbour. It's an open secret in Martinaise. Surely it must not come as a *complete* surprise to the RCM either. Perhaps it's time to look into it?"
"The Union won *significant* concessions -- including overtime pay *and* a medical plan. This time their demands are more... I guess you could say *aggressive*."
"The Zone of Control is the third incarnation of Revachol. After the failure of the Suzerain and the Commune."
"The age of capital has only begun. I will talk to my employers in person. We will amputate and cauterize Martinaise -- if you handle the situation on the ground."
"The board is not gonna like it."
"The boat? No. *It* is called Cor-de-Leite '19 -- because that's the type of sloop it is."
"The company did not 'send mercenaries after the Union'. I told you, in great detail, about the mistakes my side made. And of course I accept them completely."
"The company has tried looking into this matter before -- to no avail. Perhaps someone with *your* authority and resources might turn over the right stones?"

"The eighth expedition returned, sane and intact. They told of a new continent of matter. They told the queen and her councillor, Dolores Dei, that the pale had begun to condense, day after day, hour after hour, minute after minute."
"The first living, autonomous organism. Proof of reality. It's the symbol of Insulinde, detective, the coat-of-arms of the Suzerain and the wings on the crest of the Commune."
"The further into pale you travel, the steeper the degree of suspension. Right down to the mathematical -- *numbers* stop working. No one has yet passed the number barrier. It may be impossible."
"The girl in the old-lady rags?"
"The goal posts have moved, lieutenant. In the absence of the badge I have informed my employer there will be a probe."
"The information I'm to share with you includes sensitive trade secrets. For the sake of my employer, I have to ask for your name and badge number."
"The liberals got the mineral rights." She looks up to the sky, then inland at the crumbling city. "And by mineral rights, I mean *everything*."
"The liberals took everything that wasn't nailed to the ground -- the Coalition took the *ground*," she stomps her rubber booted foot. "The ocean, the laws and the people."
"The lieutenant's right, let's change topics?" She gives you a little wink: "What do you want to know? Anything!"
"The logical positivists say -- the dialectical materialists argue."
"The lorries are still stuck at the roundabout -- if the police is asking, one of the drivers might admit to it."
"The moralists believe in keeping everything exactly the way it is. They believe in mineral rights -- and not shooting people in the head..."
"The nations of Mundi proceeded to discover five more isolae -- or they discovered us -- all in the rush of the great interisolary reconnection..."
"The nations of the Occident. Or migrant workers from Semenine and Iilmaraa, depending on your creed."

"The nations who colonized this isola called theirs *Mundi*. The World. It was all they knew, all they thought would be. That there would be something more was a gamble. Akin to another world -- or life after death."
"The other time I *would* have finished the race were it not for an urgent work matter, much like the one I'm on now."
"The pale is not, technically speaking, part of *reality*..."
"The pale outweighs reality two to one -- there is more pale than there is matter. And the ratio is slipping."

"The pale was thought to be impregnable, perpetual." She points northwest. "Irene La Navigateur, the Queen of Suresne, sent *eight* expeditions, one after the other, into the mass at the edge of the world. Five of the crews did not return. Two did, but had lost their minds."
"The point of the presentation is -- these kinds of things *happen* around the Claires. Watch out when you're dealing with him."

"The post-revolutionary decade was a disaster for the Coalition Government. Revachol in the Twenties was hell, especially on the west side of the river: gang warfare, a botched privatisation scheme, a nuclear pile meltdown..."
"The real king abdicated and lived out a long and productive life as a venture capitalist in Graad."
"The remaining contractors. Their *tribunal*. It's what they believe."
"The sailor's soul would use it to fly back home if they should die abroad. This is a sort of... contraption. To be reeled back in by. The *silver cord*, they would call it."

"The same strict psychological regimen the eighth admiral developed when he crossed the pale and discovered this isola -- the *Volta do Mar*. It's used by interisolary travellers and other troubled souls even to this day."
"The situation is *extremely* volatile. The sooner we can speak about this lynching business, the better for all of us."
"The sooner the probe is finished the sooner I can share *crucial* information with you." She takes a sip of tea. "Now, is there anything I can do for you in the meanwhile? Tea, perhaps?"

"The story is, one of them, the colonel -- I don't know his real name -- sexually assaulted a local woman. While he was drunk and separated from his unit. This allowed some of the more militant Union members to subdue him."
"The strike brew," she nods. "That's a classic. And by *turn up the heat* I presume you mean *put more alcohol in it*?"
"The times have changed."
"The two *might* even be connected."
"The... *scabs*?" She raises her brow. "You mean the huddled masses of Jamrock, come to plead for work where the Union refuses to?"
"Then certainly you must know that under the Wayfarer Act the RCM doesn't have the authority to demand anyone's operator license. Freedom of movement and all that."

"Then he made his way to the Preto Grande, through what I think must be Staadskanaal -- an artificial channel through the Occident. From the Preto he sailed to the Insulindic ocean. First the Semenese islands, then this..." She points to his heart.
"Then tell me -- what do you *think* of the pale?"
"Then there's the matter of that little scamp in old-lady clothes. She threatened to paint the Cor-de-Leite red. Like blood, you see. Well, I like it the way it is -- white."
"Then they don't."
"Then we're on the same page -- as grim as it may be."
"Then we're talking about a *war*. Evrart needs to let me into the harbour at once. We need to talk about this."
"Then what does that say?" She points to the plaque on the side of the pier. "Does it say *docking reserved for residents of Rue de Saint-Ghislaine 33A*?"
"Then what is this positively destitute *jetty* doing here?" She puts her foot down on the rotten planks beneath. "And what about that fleet of skiffs?"
"Then you might also like their other slogan: 'DEMAND DEMOCRACY!'"
"Then you would have died fighting against them. Long before the Beachhead... our time is a shadow cast by that day."
"Then you would have died, most likely. Not far from here -- maybe even *right* here, during the Beachhead, defending the coast the day the Coalition took the city."

"There *are* signs of pretermodern crossings. Successful navigation of the pale relies not just on technical know-how, but intensive psychological preparation. Some of these tactics have been known for thousands of years."
"There are leaflets everywhere, and banners... what did they say again? Oh, yes..."
"There are those who would call it *Hell*..."
"There is a term of endearment they coined for it. In the Dolorian century, when humanity was *high* on this world, discovering more and more of it -- these archipelagos included..."
"There may be *some* detectives who are not philosophers."

"There was no one but the skua. The Liliacea. And the blood beech and the River Esperance. It was the New New World. The Mondials used it to amass the greatest concentration of wealth mankind has ever seen -- Revachol the Suzerain."
"There will be no *gloaming*. There will be slow, simmering, hideous civil war. The beginnings of a failed state. No rapture, just ugliness."
"There's a steadily increasing trickle of images. Between the big three scientific contributors, they're piecing together a dark grey corona."
"There's a steadily increasing trickle of images. Between the big three they're piecing together a dark grey corona."
"There's nothing *basic* about your role, detective. It's true that the RCM keeps everything the way our seemingly *permanent* provisional rulers like it..." She leans in.
"These are... unimportant times, detective." She puts her finger to her lips, then points at you: "You and I were born after the dust had settled, a thousandth of a second too late."
"These men work in tandem using semi-and fully automatic firearms. Their armour is virtually impenetrable to muzzle-loaded weapons -- even *yours*. Most Union workers don't have guns at all..."
"They are having a blast -- but how can they *afford* it? After four months my assumption was they would prefer a more *practical* solution."
"They are what they are -- who knows, an afterbloom may yet come..."

"They boast a long list of clients: Saint-Batiste, Welchman-Lorentz, Eendracht... A warning sign, however -- the operations concerned all take place in third- or fourth-world countries. Guarding facilities, escort missions, and such."
"They call it *the blend-over of the self*. The pale does not only suspend the laws of physics, but also the laws of psychology, maybe History, even... The human mind becomes over-radiated by past."

"They called it the *International Zone* -- because no nation wanted to claim responsibility. The RCM restored peace where the Coalition failed. A true-blue citizens' initiative," she smiles. "They will never forgive you."
"They didn't *win* so much as survive. *We* were the last ones standing when the war ended -- everyone else got shot in the head, remember?"
"They don't have the same respect for the Revachol Citizens Militia as I do. To put it bluntly they think you're vigilantes, *ghetto savages*. It will not be a fruitful meeting."
"They have the support of Revachol West. They have the position... this will be a prolonged and bloody conflict. The only question is how long -- and how bloody." She falls silent.
"They most certainly are not." Her eyes return to you. "Krenel has a thousand men on their payroll. The next batch will be a platoon of twenty men and a gunship."
"They picked the winning side. That's why they're here and others are not."
"They say it's where the *terrible* questions of our time will be answered -- the tensions are highest, the faultlines deepest."

"They say there is a rarefied envelope of matter surrounding the darkened disc of our planet. That is, if we are still living on a planet. Or, to speak more plainly, imagine vast swathes of land disrupted by nothingness."

"They started as an exploration and cargo fleet conducting trade between the Samaran and Insulindian isolas -- 250 years ago, when Pines' ships explored the South-Semenese and charted Lo Manthang on behalf of the suzerain."

"They wear ceramic armour, have semi-automatic weapons and years of combat experience. They also have Trauma-and-Stressor Disorder and no idea how to conduct themselves in an urban civilian environment."
"They were dispatched after I relayed the Union's initial offer."
"They will last as long as the drug trade in Jamrock provides them with support. With all due respect, that will be a long and bloody time."
"They're *nonsense*, a load of tripe." She tosses back her hair. "But we were on the subject of the talks I believe."
"They're *not*. That's the problem. The Union stopped all negotiations a week ago. After that awful lynching took place."
"They're like you and I, I suppose. Living organisms don't identify with abstractions. Elysium is for particular beings."
"They've gone to ground, as it were. I don't recommend seeking them out." She puts her foot on the guardwire, for balance. "For one -- they're almost certainly armed to the teeth."
"Think nothing of it, officer." She runs her hand along the fibreglass cabin. "What's a little *class conflict* between friends?"
"This *place* is an unmarked microsettlement on the coast of Martinaise..." She gestures toward a collection of cinderblock dwellings covered by a highly carcinogenic roofing material.

"This is a limited-time opportunity. Once the complaint has been processed by the trade committee they'll have no choice but to lower the drawbridge -- and the operation will continue." She looks north.
"This is their Zone of Control. They embolden the RCM with crumbs of the same law they took. Technically speaking -- *you* are a moralist."
"This isn't really an inquiry, is it? You can't remember a single thing -- this is the first time you're hearing about any of this."

"This one used to be eight to ten stories tall -- a real high rise by the standards of the last century. Built to mirror the skyscrapers across the bay in the Delta. That was before the war, of course."
"This place could use a competent manager. There's so much to be done. But then, I'll never get around to it, will I?"
"This place hasn't changed at all."
"This thing is what you call a..." she pronounces the word with sudden carelessness: "*clusterfuck*. I am saddened to hear the news, of course. But we must continue. Lest the situation worsens."
"This unmistakably *proletarian* fleet of skiffs." She waves at the nearby fishing boats. "As I said, *plenty* of people drive boats. Of all social strata."
"This... *reality*?" She pulls her hood closer around her neck.

"Those days are long behind me..." She looks inland with sarcastic wistfulness. "And even in the early Thirties I would say I was more of a *New* girl. Disco was a minor, but still enjoyable facet of the whole thing for me."
"Those would be the communists. Generally speaking, 40 million people got shot in the head during the World Revolution. But the communists -- they *all* got shot in the head."
"Thousands of litres of raw ingredients will pour onto the streets of Revachol. Not the East, across the river, but the West. The vulnerable, the weary..."
"Time flies."

"To answer your question -- yes. They were organized by Wild Pines. The contractors picked them up from Jamrock and drove them over. This is standard practice. The company reserves a right to man its stations."
"To foreign intervention -- the Coalition. Those people *really* took the mineral rights."
"To think I even used to go dancing here."
"Too many things have *already* gone wrong." She looks to you, eyes damp from the wind.
"Too much *reality* at once can prove too much," she nods. "There's plenty of time later. For now, is there anything *else* I can help you with?"
"Truly moralist of you. The Coalition Government would applaud you for staying out of politics. And yet..."
"Trust me, officer, I am *fully committed* to resolving this impasse. This isn't some *side gig* for me."
"Try again, dear. A little lower this time."

"Twenty billion is a large number, but the conglomerate employs 72,000 people. They all need to be paid. Then there are capital improvements, interest payments..." A wave hits the sloop, she grasps the mainstay for balance.
"Twenty-two kilometres from the centre of the world. That soldering iron is the Bank of the World building. The bottom floors are INSURCOM -- *Coalition Government* Insulindian Mission Command."
"Typically arrogant of me.... Absent-minded as well. Interisolary travel has left holes in my consciousness, I'm afraid."
"Uhm..." She seems confused. "I meant *you* -- the Revachol Citizens Militia. The police."
"Uhm..." The woman dips her fingers back into the bag. "I really did bring as little cash as possible, to avoid attention. So here you are, the last of bit of filthy *lucre* I can share."
"Understandable," she nods.
"Unfortunate." She shakes her head. "I won't pry further into the details of your investigation, but let me just say -- I have *full* trust in your competence."
"Unimportant, as I said. The mineral rights were all distributed during the Revolution -- as were the bullets to the heads."

"Unlikely, officer. I'm talking about the lorries. Once the ingredients reach Jamrock they're distributed to a network of local manufacturers, well beyond our grasp. But in transit they may be *vulnerable*."
"Until after *years* of trial and error -- and the development of a *strict* psychological regime imitating the creation process of poetry..."
"Until the executions start? Truthfully -- I don't know. It depends on their progress identifying the members of the lynch mob. And their impatience."
"Until then -- is there anything *I* can help *you* with?"
"Until you come up with something at that intersection I'm afraid I have little else to tell you -- but I'll try. Ask."
"Up to my gills, officer."
"Very absurd," she nods. "Thank you for the suggestion. I will stick with the factory name for now -- but thank you."
"Very curious." She blinks both eyes. "A very curious thing to do."
"Very keen of you, officer. I do also have *saudetic syndrome* from overexposure to the pale. It makes me roost in the night. Like an owl."
"Very rugged," she nods in approval. "Good choice. Now, I suspect you had questions -- nothing like talking to pass a rainy day, am I right?"
"Villiers & La Salle was one of the original 14 indotribes of Revachol, did you know? Artillery and ballistics. Before the Revolution of course, they belong to some Gottwalders now."
"Voracious," she nods approvingly. "I'm up for it. What'll it be?"
"Was there something else you wanted to know? I remember something about a low-down..."
"Wasn't it Guillaume le Million who said: *If you can remember the New, you weren't there*?"
"We *did*, on more than one occasion. Apparently there's some sort of inter-precinct disagreement about whose jurisdiction this area falls under."

"We are standing on a fertile, self-sufficient island able to sustain up to 200 million people; in the middle of the Insulindic ocean -- the world's connective tissue..." She smiles. "It's where the money is."
"We are where we are. I have no truer answer to give, unfortunately." She watches you closely as you scan the horizon.
"We are. And the city of Revachol is on the island of Le Caillou."
"We built this district," she says, calmly.
"We contain multitudes, do we not? It might not be pertinent to her... *profession*, but who knows? It may help you find her yet."
"We do for this," she nods.
"We may be here awhile, then." She takes a long sip of tea. "Ask away, officer -- I'll help however I can."
"We may be here awhile, then." She takes a long sip to clear her throat. "Ask away, officer -- I'll help however I can."

"We surrendered the nation to financial colonists. No sane person identifies as an *ultra* anymore. Not in broad daylight." She looks you in the eye. "Tell me -- now that I've *uncoiled* myself -- are you repulsed?"
"We told ourselves we were the worst thing to happen to the coast since the Coalition landed in '08. Imagine!" She tosses her head.

"We used to think it was a sphere, but that is beginning to look less and less likely by the day. You wouldn't know it from the tabloids, but the ORG nations have been launching weather balloons into the lower ionosphere since the Thirties."
"We will see."
"We're in Martinaise, baby."
"We're in logistics. It's our business to know -- and no. As far as the company knows, the Union does not produce it. They transport the ingredients. For a cut."
"Weird? Oh no. One of the positive things to come from the Revolution is the *unhindered* exchange of information, you see, even when it comes to *trade secrets*..."
"Welcome to reality, baby."
"Well then. Reality *is* a strange place -- getting stranger by the day. Ask away, officer. I'll help however I can."

"Why *Dolores*?"
"Why do you think so?" Her voice is calm, there is only curiosity there.
"Why not?" She tosses her head. "I've heard the analogy made by a blindingly modern school of philosophy called *karperie*. It may not be as far fetched as it sounds."
"Why of course -- we're talking duke-out central. Full-swing intraspecies warfare."
"Why wouldn't it be? This is Revachol. Wayfarer act and all. *Anyone* can drive a boat."
"Why yes, I am rich. How much money do you need? Hopefully not too much, I couldn't bring all of it with me."
"Why, by throwing off half a century of foreign domination under the Coalition! Unfortunately for you, the Coalition also leases you the right to police West Revachol..."
"Why, if I may ask? Why make them *more* drunk? Aren't they corked enough already?"
"Why, thank you." She does not register the real meaning of the remark.
"Why, yes I am..." She looks at the deck under her feet. Green and white sails flutter overhead.
"Why, you and I, officer--" She spreads her arms, raincoat flapping in the wind. "Our lives in the Zone of Control."
"Wild Pines employs 72,000 people, all of whom have families that depend on their salaries. It is a tremendous responsibility."
"With all due respect to these desert cacti, the contents of a few cash registers cannot provide for *two-thousand* men. The local businesses can scarcely provide for themselves."
"With due respect to our overlords, the eternal *caretaker* government that keeps Martinaise a monument to the efficacy of its artillery..."
"Wonderful."
"Word has travelled, yes, but nothing of real substance has surfaced yet, I gather?" She smiles, then explains: "Wild Pines has eyes on the intersection -- but not ears."
"Yes -- Insulinde."
"Yes -- Jean-Luc *Measurehead*." She leans back and rolls her eyes.
"Yes -- and? Will you start an official investigation?"
"Yes -- anyway." She adjusts her hair. The permanent wave in her auburn locks radiates victory.
"Yes -- but please don't call me that."
"Yes -- so I can spite Evrart and spoil his plans for this place. I'm a petty person, I admit."
"Yes -- that is enough. Many cities are built *much* closer."
"Yes -- the red deluge. The *Insulindian Deluge* they call it."
"Yes -- you and I belong to the supraculture. We're common, the herd. The music on the radio, the food in the chain restaurant -- those are all too *popular* for the girl in the old-lady rags."
"Yes!" She claps her hands for warmth.
"Yes, I believe there is a connection -- but that's a subject for *later*." Her eyes narrow.
"Yes, I suppose I am. But I wouldn't be a patriot anywhere but here."
"Yes, I was *slumming* it with some girl-friends of mine. We had boats and..." She smiles. "Don't hold it against me -- my *paramour* certainly did not."
"Yes, I was *slumming* it with some girlfriends of mine. We had boats and..." She smiles. "Don't hold it against me -- the boys certainly did not."
"Yes, King Guillaume had a nose for bad PR. He ran before it -- what is the expression -- *went down*? Anyway, Gil got out alive and his nephew Frissel got shot in his place..."
"Yes, an acute thiamine deficiency can be exacerbated by alcoholism." She blinks her green eyes. "Exacerbated means 'made worse.'"
"Yes, extremely. Keep in mind, this is a negotiator Mr. Claire has worked with before, and who was more than fair with him and the Union."
"Yes, let's..." She settles down -- still a quivering smile on her face.
"Yes, lieutenant. Permit me to conclude with this -- *who* you are -- to me -- is the police. The only legitimate law enforcement authority in Revachol."
"Yes, my eyes on the harbour have sent word to that effect -- what have you discovered?"
"Yes, past a certain point numbers begin to seem *imaginary*. But they are quite real for the 72,000 employees who depend on Wild Pines for their pay checks..."
"Yes, sweet reality," she stomps her foot. "But before we do, tell me detective..."
"Yes, we are." She raises her brow. "We are on Le Caillou."
"Yes, whatever else I am, I'm also a mother. And a wife." She closes her eyes, then opens them again. "Now -- shall we return to reality?"
"Yes, yes, Mr. Evrart... this gossiping idea was terrible on my part, I take it back."
"Yes," she leans slightly closer: "That's the talk about town. The *Hardie boys* they're called..." A crooked smile returns to her face. "I find the name rather amusing, honestly."
"Yes," she nods slowly. "I am the nether creature of the forbidden swamp. I pushed the king under a *shitwagon* and betrayed the Revolution. My kind surrendered the nation to financial colonists..."
"Yes. After they clear the terminal we lose track. The actual production is taking place at various sites in and around Jamrock Quarter. North of here."
"Yes. All the good conflict corridors: Supramundi, Yeesut, the Semenese islands. Countries that don't have a good record reporting *atrocious* military conduct on their soil."
"Yes. And quantitative easing. It was a market mirage, unfortunately. The Forties dispelled it. An isola-wide hangover, you might say. So, here we are..." She curtsies.
"Yes. But you won't get anything out of Evrart and the Dockworkers' Union. Still --" she raises her bony finger, "every chain has its weak link."
"Yes. Carried in the hulls of airships," she nods. "It's a horrific job. Automation will abolish it, soon."
"Yes. Edgar looks *exactly* like his brother, except for that lazy eye. He also *talks* exactly like Evrart does. And when one's term as foreman is up, the other takes over."
"Yes. Evrart is a showman at heart."
"Yes. I'm afraid this strike may descend into a small scale civil war. With possible consequences for all of Revachol West."
"Yes. I'm sad I will never have the time, detective -- I've always wanted a dilapidating fishing village."
"Yes. Keep in mind, this is a negotiator Mr. Claire has worked with before, and who was more than fair with him and the Union."
"Yes. Mr. Claire has a two-month head start. I can't let it grow any bigger. And I've exhausted all my options from here."
"Yes. On the last day of the local chapter elections her daughter phoned in and said she wasn't running anymore -- or coming to work. Ever. End of story."
"Yes. That means: not de jure. The RCM acts in what is poetically called the *twilight of international law*; both at the behest of the Coalition Government -- and to its chagrin."
"Yes. The *Insulindian Deluge* they call it."
"Yes. They were organized by Wild Pines. The contractors picked them up from Jamrock and drove them over. This is standard practice. The company reserves a right to man its stations."
"Yes. We are on an island in an ocean. The world's largest body of water -- the Insulindic."

"Yes." She pauses. "Pale covers 72% of the surface. There are grey flares and prominences, even arcs above entire isolas... The images are blurry, but if there was a sphere in there it certainly looks like it fractured a long time ago."
"Yes."

"Yes?"

"You're not alone. Neither do most of these people -- the literacy rate is around 45% west of the river. Fifty years of occupation have left these people in an *oblivion* of poverty."

"Young people who dye their hair funny colours and wear old people's clothes are stupid and their little rebellion is self-defeating..."
"Your colleague, Lieutenant Kitsuragi, is competent. I checked up on him. And you have me -- I will try to assist you in any way I can."
